purpose: Which CapabilityObjective governs each tenant's capability units. Teleon runs the same capability for many tenants; each prioritizes differently, so placement (which runtime class) and the non-deterministic->deterministic descent follow the TENANT's priority. A binding is either {"objective_preset": <preset>} or {"weights": {...}}. A tenant with no binding gets default_objective_preset. Data only (read by src/teleon/objectives/tenant_binding.py) — never a code path; never names a src.baltor symbol.

baltor-compliance.rationale: regulated-fact tenant — accuracy/determinism over cost; the lossless-distillation law as a priority: never trade answer-critical accuracy for a cheaper rule on novel inputs

high-volume-batch.rationale: high-volume background enrichment — cost is the binding constraint; descend to deterministic rules aggressively

interactive-assistant.rationale: user-facing interactive surface — latency is the binding constraint; prefer tight-SLA placements

determinism-first-audit.rationale: auditable/reproducible pipeline — runs must be deterministic and replayable for the receipt trail

llm-budget-capped.rationale: a tenant on a hard model-call budget — minimize LLM usage, prefer template/deterministic runners

cost-accuracy-blend.name: cost-accuracy-blend
cost-accuracy-blend.rationale: an explicit custom weight policy (not a preset) — a tenant that wants cost AND accuracy balanced above latency/llm
